cover.title: He hung them for her. For 50 years.

lines.text: He hung dolls for fifty years. For a dead girl.
Xochimilco, Mexico City. A maze of old canals and floating gardens, south of the city.
On one tiny island lived a man named Don Julián Santana. Alone, for decades.
He told people that a young girl drowned in the canal right by his island.
And soon after... he found a doll, floating in the water.
He hung it in a tree, to honor her. Then he hung another. And another.
For about fifty years, he pulled dolls out of the trash and out of the canals. Hundreds of them.
On trees. On fences. Hanging from the roof of his shack. Some say he believed they kept her spirit at peace.
Then, in April 2001, his nephew found Don Julián face down in the canal. Dead.
Reports say he was found in the same spot where he said the girl had died.
No record of the girl has ever been found. But his family kept the island... and the dolls.
Today, boats take tourists there. The dolls are still hanging. Rotting in the sun and the rain.
Would you spend a night there? Comment I'd go, or not a chance. Sleep tight, partner.
